deliverables: Milestone-based disbursement controls through Intersect smart contract process
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, with later transfer to a Project-Specific Smart Contract when legal contract and vendor readiness conditions are met.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continuous development through Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: Mithril uses stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way so nodes and applications can verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
The requested budget is 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development plus a 110,983 ada Intersect Budget Administration fee, totaling 3,810,423 ada.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested withdrawal does not, at the time of submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
Audit and oversight costs are included within the overhead applied to this proposal, and Intersect's administration fee covers administrative oversight.
Independent oversight will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, including reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs.
Teragone has worked on Mithril for several years through collaboration with IOG, which has funded the project to date.

Intersect will use a 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract, with specified admin, leadership, and trusted-entity approval thresholds for funding, disbursement, pause/resume, sweep, and reorganize actions.
A treasury.sundae.fi dashboard is available for the community to audit and track the withdrawn ada, with metrics also immutably verifiable on chain.

summary: The document requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration, describes broad technical and ecosystem rationale, references Intersect budget voting and smart-contract oversight materials, and provides treasury-management addresses and control thresholds, but does not include a complete proposal summary, detailed budget analysis, feasibility assessment, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, or failure-mode analysis.
